newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia govt tightens pharmaceutical scheme.
newsitem.headline: Australia govt tightens pharmaceutical scheme.

text.p: The Australian government said on Tuesday it planned to tighten spending on its pharmaceutical benefits scheme, resulting in expected savings of about A$696 million over the next four years.
"PBS outlays doubled in the last five years and such a rate of growth is clearly unsustainable," Health Minister Michael Wooldridge said in a statement accompanying budget papers.

The government plans to cut around A$560 million over four years through the introduction of a base price scheme for similar drugs. Under the scheme, any patient who chooses a more expensive drug than the base price drug will pay the difference.
It would also save about A$112 million over the four year period through the deletion from the PBS schedule of a number of drugs used to treat less serious medical conditions.
In addition, A$24 million should be saved through the establishment of a National Provider Service from March 1998, which would lead to more appropriate prescribing.
Under the current PBS system, the cost of numerous drugs -- for example, insulin -- is heavily subsidised by the government to bring down the price charged to patients.
